en: The Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty.
When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, he clearly perceived the five [aggregates]...
All aggregates are empty; they transcend all suffering and calamity. "Śāriputra!
Form is not different from emptiness, and emptiness is not different from form; form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself form."
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also like this. "Śāriputra!
These dharmas have the characteristic of emptiness: they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure, neither increasing nor decreasing."
Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no sensation, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
and no forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects.
There is no眼界 (eye-element), up to and including no意識界 (consciousness-element);
there is no ignorance nor the extinction of ignorance, up to and including no old age and death nor the extinction of old age and death;
there is no suffering, origin, cessation, or path.
There is no ignorance, and there is nothing to be attained.
Because there is nothing to be attained, the Bodhisattva relies on the Prajñāpāramitā; thus, the mind is without hindrance.
Because there is no hindrance, there is no fear; being far removed from perverted dreams and delusions, one reaches ultimate Nirvāṇa.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time, by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā, have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Therefore, know that the Prajñāpāramitā is the great divine mantra, the great illuminating mantra, the unsurpassed mantra, the unequaled mantra; it is able to eliminate all suffering, for it is true and not false. Thus, the Prajñāpāramitā mantra is spoken.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
"Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. —The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom.
